# n8n: Stored credentials (third-party secrets held by n8n)

`n8n-5` · API key / token · service. Secrets for external services saved in n8n and used by workflow nodes. A compromised n8n account or API key can use them through workflows; the API does not return secret values.

Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant. "No docs found" means vendor documentation does not say either way.

| Question | Answer | Why | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Identify: Admin can list all of them | Yes | GET /api/v1/credentials lists all credentials on the instance for owner/admin. | GET /api/v1/credentials lists all credentials on the instance for owner/admin. |
| Protect: Admin can block or require approval | No docs found | No documented control found. |  |
| Protect: SSO and MFA rules apply | No docs found | No vendor documentation found. |  |
| Protect: IP restriction | Conditional | Allowed HTTP Request Domains limits where a credential can be sent from the HTTP Request node only; not a source-IP control. | Allowed HTTP Request Domains: Credential modal > Allowed HTTP Request Domains |
| Protect: Expires automatically | No docs found | Set by the external service |  |
| Detect: Usage appears in logs | Yes | not documented | Where: Settings > Log Streaming > Events: Audit (User credentials created/shared/updated/deleted) and Workflow (n8n.workflow.*, by workflowId) |
| Detect: Data reads appear in logs | No docs found | No collection call researched. |  |
| Respond: Revocation ends active access | No docs found | Rotate the secret at the external service, then update or delete the n8n credential. |  |
| Respond: Stops working when user is removed | Partial | On user deletion the admin chooses to transfer the user's credentials to another user or delete them; the secret stays valid at the external service either way. | Where: Settings > Users > three-dot menu > Delete user > transfer or delete their credentials; then rotate the secret at the external service · API: DELETE /api/v1/users/{userId}?transferId={projectId} (omit transferId to delete credentials) |

## Protect: what an admin can configure

### Admin controls
- **Credential type policy** (Limit resources; all plans; default unknown). Instance or project rules for which credential types are allowed. Where: PUT /credential-type-policies/instance.
- **Allowed HTTP Request Domains** (Limit network; all plans; default unknown). Limits which domains a credential can be sent to from the HTTP Request node. Where: Credential modal > Allowed HTTP Request Domains.

- Network: conditional (checked at api_request). Allowed HTTP Request Domains limits where a credential can be sent from the HTTP Request node only; not a source-IP control.
- Lifetime: Set by the external service. Renewal: Rotate at the external service and update the credential.
- Keyless option: not_applicable. Depends on the external service.
- Conditions: Plan for credential type policy not stated.

## Detect: what gets logged
- Token prefix: not established

### Logs
- Log streaming (Audit group): Enterprise.

### Fields that identify the credential
- `not documented` (User credentials * events): 

### Lifecycle events
- create: `User credentials created` 
- other: `User credentials shared` 
- revoke: `User credentials deleted` 

### Correlate on
`userId`, `workflowId`

### API calls a holder can make, and whether they are logged
- enumeration (bulk): `GET /api/v1/credentials`. Credential names and types, not secrets Logged: unknown. 

### What to look for (analyst guidance)
- Credential shared or transferred to a new project
- New workflow using HTTP Request node with a credential set to All domains

## Respond: how to revoke it


Rotate the secret at the external service, then update or delete the n8n credential. Live access ends on revocation: unknown.
